text: The paddock glowed with evening's honey light.
Sunny hopped along the winding track.
Beside the track, a mob of kangaroos
was settling slowly down to rest.
And from a mama's pouch there peeped a joey,
with great long ears and eyes like midnight pools.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a cosy bed!”
“The cosiest,” he squeaked. “It's warm as toast!”
He wriggled and he turned and snuggled down,
till only ears were poking from the pouch.
“My mama's pouch goes everywhere I go,
so I am always home,” he told her proudly.
The mama kangaroo bent down her head,
and nuzzled both the little ones goodnight.
The mob grew still across the silver grass,
like gentle boulders resting in the moon.
The joey gave a tiny sleepy yawn,
and disappeared inside his woolly home.
Just one soft ear still peeked into the night,
to hear the mama's heartbeat drumming slow.
Sunny found a tussock soft and round,
and curled up in the moon-washed silver grass.
The paddock hushed. The mob breathed slow and deep.
Everything was peaceful, warm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy in the honey dark.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping mob,
dreaming of a pouch as warm as toast.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little joey.
Goodnight, sleepy mob. Goodnight, little one.
